text:
Teeth of flowers, bonnet of dew,

hands of grasses, you, fine nurse,

have ready for me the earthy sheets

and the comforter of weeded mosses.


I am going to sleep, my nurse, lay me down.

Put a lamp at my headboard;

a constellation; whichever you like;

all are good; lower it a little.


Leave me alone: you hear the buds breaking...

a celestial foot rocks you from above

and a bird traces some measures for you


so that you forget... Thank you. Ah, one errand:

if he calls again by telephone

tell him not to insist, that I have gone out...

translation.title: I Am Going to Sleep
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the lullaby plainness and the famous final telephone instruction.
